# Marginalia

> Marginalia is a self-hosted writing tool for long-form fiction co-written with large language models. You write the instructions for each part of the

- [Marginalia](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/index.md): Marginalia
- [User guide](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/index.md): This part of the manual is for people who write with Marginalia and for those who run it for others. It explains every screen and setting, from installing Marginalia and connecting a model to branching a story, building a lorebook and backing up the database.
- [Developer guide](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/index.md): This part of the manual is for people who want to change Marginalia itself, write an extension for it, or just understand how it works inside. If you only want to install and use Marginalia, see the User guide.
- [Credits](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/credits.md): The screenshots in this manual that show a picture of a part (for example in the story editor, the Images dialog, the Resources tab and the backup dialogs)

## User guide

### Getting started

- [Getting started](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/getting-started/index.md): Marginalia runs in your browser. You can install it in two ways:
- [Desktop app](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/getting-started/desktop-app.md): The desktop app is a self-contained version of Marginalia for one computer. It brings its own Java runtime and server, listens only on your computer and opens in your default browser.
- [Server (Docker)](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/getting-started/docker-server.md): Run Marginalia as a server when several people use it, or when you want to open it from other devices. Every user gets their own books, lorebooks, inference providers and protocols.
- [First start](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/getting-started/first-start.md): When Marginalia starts with an empty database, it asks for the first account instead of showing the login screen. This account is the administrator: it can manage users, database backups, cleanup and extensions.
- [Quick start](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/getting-started/quick-start.md): From a fresh installation to the first generated part of a story. It assumes Marginalia is installed and you are logged in as the administrator.
- [Inference providers](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/inference-providers.md): An inference provider is a connection to a model: the API address, the API key, the model and its limits. Every book uses one provider. You can have as many as you like, for example a large cloud model for the story and a small local one for experiments, and switch a book between them at any time.
- [Protocols](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/protocols.md): A protocol is a set of generation settings: the sampling parameters (temperature, top P and penalties) and, optionally, its own context and reply limits. The inference provider says which model writes; the protocol says how.

### Books

- [Books](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/books/index.md): A book is one story. You give it instructions part by part, the model writes the text, and the book keeps everything that goes with it: the story tree with all its branches, the prompts that shape the style, the lorebook with the world and characters, summaries and backups.
- [Managing books](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/books/managing-books.md): The Books tab lists your books. Other users' books are not shown.
- [Story editor](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/books/story-editor.md): The Story tab of a book is where you write. It shows the parts of the active branch from the beginning to the end.
- [Branches & story tree](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/books/branches-and-story-tree.md): Marginalia never makes you throw a version away. Every alternative you try is kept as a branch of the story, and you can go back to any of them.
- [Book prompts](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/books/prompts.md): The Prompts tab of a book holds the texts Marginalia builds the prompt from: two templates, the narrative settings and the summary prompts. They decide the voice of the book far more than the model settings do.
- [Summaries](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/books/summaries.md): A model can only read a limited amount of text at once (its context). When a book grows beyond that, Marginalia leaves out the oldest parts, and the model forgets what happened in them.
- [Exporting a book](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/books/export.md): Export turns the story into a file you can read, print, send or publish elsewhere. Unlike a backup it contains only the text, as a finished book.
- [Book backups](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/books/backups.md): A book backup is a snapshot of one book: its settings and prompts, all parts in all branches, summaries, tags and the lorebook. Use backups to go back to an earlier state of the story, to make a copy of a book, or to move a book to another Marginalia installation or user.
- [Publishing & viewer](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/books/publishing.md): The viewer is a reading view of your books: just the text of the story, without the editor around it. It works well on phones and tablets. Publishing a book lets other users of the same Marginalia installation read it in the viewer.
- [Resources](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/resources.md): The Resources tab lists the files you have uploaded to Marginalia. For now these are the pictures of the parts of your books. The tab is the place to find a picture again, to download it, to swap it for a better one without touching the books that use it, and to throw away what you no longer need.
- [Trash](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/trash.md): Deleting in Marginalia does not destroy anything right away: a deleted book, lorebook, story part or inference provider is only marked as deleted and hidden from your lists.

### Lorebooks

- [Lorebooks](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/lorebooks/index.md): A lorebook holds what the model must know about your world: characters, places, history, rules, terminology. Each piece of knowledge is an entry. Before
- [Creating lorebooks](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/lorebooks/lorebooks.md): Open the Lorebooks tab. The editor shows one lorebook at a time; pick it in the Lorebook field at the top. Lorebooks belong to your account: other users don't see them.
- [Entries & activation](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/lorebooks/entries.md): Each row of the lorebook editor is one entry:
- [Import & export](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/lorebooks/import-export.md): Select the lorebook in the editor and click the export button (file icon, Export Lorebook). The browser downloads lorebook name.json with:

### Templates & macros

- [Templates & macros](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/templates/index.md): Everything Marginalia sends to the model is built from templates: texts with placeholders that are filled in for each generated part. You can change them all, from the frame of the prompt down to a single lorebook entry.
- [Prompt templates](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/templates/templates.md): Templates use Handlebars syntax, extended with SillyTavern macros. This page covers the variables each template gets and the Handlebars part of the syntax.
- [Macro reference](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/templates/macros.md): Marginalia understands the macros of SillyTavern, so prompts and world info written for SillyTavern work without changes. Macros work in every template: master template, user prompt, summary prompt and lorebook entries.

### Extensions

- [Extensions](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/extensions/index.md): Extensions add features to Marginalia without changing the application itself. Five extensions come with Marginalia:
- [Author's Note](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/extensions/authors-note.md): A note to the model that is sent with every generation of the book: the tone you want right now, what the current chapter is about, a reminder the model keeps forgetting.
- [Chapter Marker](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/extensions/chapter-marker.md): Turns the Outline of the story editor into a table of contents.
- [Lorebook VCS](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/extensions/lorebook-vcs.md): Revision history for lorebook entries: keep earlier versions of your lore and switch between them - for example the state of the world before and after a war, or a character at different points of the story.
- [Reviewer](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/extensions/reviewer.md): Lets the model review what you've written: reader reactions, an editor's critique, a continuity check - whatever you prompt it for. Reviews are kept with the part, next to the story, and never become part of the book.
- [Side Query](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/extensions/side-query.md): A chat with the model next to your story: ask about the plot, check continuity, brainstorm names or the next chapter - without adding anything to the book.
- [Account & settings](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/account.md): Everything you create in Marginalia belongs to your account: books, lorebooks, tags, inference providers, protocols and settings. Other users don't see them (except books you publish), and you don't see theirs.

### Administration

- [Administration](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/administration/index.md): Administrators manage the Marginalia installation: user accounts, database backups, cleanup of deleted data and extensions. The first account, created on the first start, is an administrator; it can make other users administrators too.
- [Users](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/administration/users.md): The Users tab of the admin page lists all accounts with their Username, Full Name and whether they are an Administrator.
- [Database backups](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/administration/database-backups.md): A database backup is a complete copy of the Marginalia database: all users with all their books, lorebooks, settings and extension data. Use it to protect the installation against mistakes and failures, and to move it to another computer.
- [Cleanup](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/administration/cleanup.md): When users delete something in Marginalia - a book, a story part, a lorebook, an inference provider - it disappears from their lists, but stays in the database.
- [Managing extensions](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/administration/extensions.md): The Extensions tab of the admin page installs and removes extensions for the whole installation.
- [Troubleshooting & FAQ](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/troubleshooting.md): Most problems leave a trace in the log:

## Developer guide

- [Building from source](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/building.md): This page shows how to build Marginalia, run it on your machine while you work on it, and build the plugins and this manual. Packaging for release (the Docker image, the desktop app, CI) is covered in Packaging & releases.
- [Architecture](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/architecture.md): Marginalia is one Java web application running in one JVM. There is no separate frontend project, no REST API and no external database: the browser shows Vaadin components that live on the server, the components call Spring services, and the services store everything in a single SQLite file.
- [Project structure](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/project-structure.md): A tour of the repository: what each folder and package contains and where to look when you want to change something. Architecture explains how the parts work together; this page is the map.
- [Domain model](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/domain-model.md): The entities Marginalia stores, how they relate, and the rules every entity follows: identity, ownership, soft delete, extended attributes and cleanup. Entities are in domain/model/ (base classes), domain/model/impl/ and domain/security/model/User.java.
- [Database & migrations](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/database.md): Marginalia keeps all its data in one SQLite file. The schema is created and upgraded by Flyway migrations, and Hibernate maps the entities onto it but never changes it.
- [Services](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/services.md): The service layer holds Marginalia's logic: everything the UI does to data goes through a service, and services are the main API extensions use. This page describes how services and repositories are built, how transactions and the current user work, and what each service is for.
- [Generation pipeline](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/generation-pipeline.md): How Marginalia turns the instruction panel into a new story part: the steps that build the prompt, how the prompt is fitted into the model's context, how the answer is streamed into the part, and the events extensions can use to change any of it.
- [Templating & macros](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/templating.md): Every prompt Marginalia sends is rendered from a template: the master template, the user prompt, lorebook entries and the summary prompt. Templates are Handlebars with SillyTavern-compatible macros on top.
- [User interface](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/ui.md): Marginalia's UI is written in Java with Vaadin Flow 25: the component tree lives on the server, the browser renders it with Vaadin's web components (Lumo theme, dark color scheme) and sends events back over HTTP and a push WebSocket.

### Plugin development

- [Plugin development](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/plugins/index.md): A Marginalia plugin (the user interface calls them extensions) is an OSGi bundle - a JAR with a few extra manifest headers - that Marginalia loads at runtime, without a restart.
- [Plugin basics](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/plugins/overview.md): This page covers what every plugin needs: the Maven project, the bundle activator, the MarginaliaExtension and how Marginalia loads, starts and unloads it.
- [@Extendable hooks](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/plugins/extendable.md): Most of what a plugin does starts with a decorator: an object whose onMethodEnter and onMethodLeave run before and after a method of an application class.
- [Extended attributes](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/plugins/extended-attributes.md): Plugins can't add tables or columns - there is no way to run their own Flyway migrations. Instead, every data entity carries a JSON object where a plugin can keep whatever it needs: ExtendableEntity.attributes.
- [Extending the UI](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/plugins/ui-extensions.md): Plugins add to the user interface from decorators: when a method that builds part of a screen runs, the plugin's decorator finds the component it built and adds to it.
- [Generation events](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/plugins/generation-events.md): @Extendable hooks change what the user sees; generation events change what the model sees. A plugin registers listeners with
- [Example plugin](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/plugins/example.md): This page builds a small plugin from scratch - Bookmarks, which lets you bookmark story parts - and then walks through two bundled plugins: Chapter Marker, the smallest one, and Author's Note, which changes the prompt sent to the model.
- [Testing](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/testing.md): Marginalia's tests are integration tests first: most of them start the real Spring XML configuration against a throwaway SQLite database and talk to a fake OpenAI-compatible server.
- [Packaging & releases](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/packaging.md): Marginalia is built once as a WAR and then shipped in two forms: a Docker image for servers and a desktop app with its own Java runtime and Jetty. This page describes how each is built, what CI does, and how a release is made.
- [Contributing](https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/developer/contributing.md): Contributions are welcome: bug reports, fixes, new features, extensions, and corrections to this manual. This page describes how to report a problem, how changes are made and what a pull request should contain.
